blocks.content: Extreme qualifiers such as 'always', 'never', and 'only' often signal incorrect statements in objective questions.

rows: Reading the full question prompt including 'NOT' or 'INCORRECT'
Skimming the question and selecting the first matching factual option
Treating extreme statements with skepticism during elimination
Assuming absolute statements ('always', 'never') are factually sound
Skipping difficult questions to return to them at the end
Spending 5+ minutes on a single question out of stubbornness
Converting units into standard formats before calculations
Directly plugging given numbers into formulas without checking units

items: Questions containing 'NOT CORRECT' cause over 15% of avoidable negative marks in competitive exams.
Distractor options often feature correct numerical calculations based on incorrect or un-converted units.
Double-check option letters before finalizing on the Computer-Based Test (CBT) portal to prevent mis-clicks.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Always read negative qualifiers like 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', and 'EXCEPT' carefully before choosing an option.
Extreme qualifiers such as 'always', 'never', and 'only' often signal incorrect statements in objective questions.
Avoid spending more than 1 to 2 minutes on a single tricky question to protect overall exam time management.
Verify unit conversions (e.g., km/h to m/s) in quantitative aptitude questions before finalizing your answer.
